abstract: We evaluate whether deposit insurance (DI) promotes liquidity by influencing depositor behavior. We use the postal savings (PS) system and state‐adopted DI schemes during the 1920s to examine the effect of bank suspensions on PS deposit growth in pairs of border cities (DI versus non‐DI). After a nearby bank suspension, (i) deposits in non‐DI‐PS offices increase sevenfold compared to deposits in adjacent DI‐PS offices, and (ii) county‐level deposits per bank decline in non‐DI counties but not in adjacent DI counties. In both cases, the effect steadily declines through the 1920s, consistent with the decreasing viability of the DI schemes.
abstract_zh: 我们评估存款保险（DI）是否通过影响储户行为来促进流动性。我们利用1920年代的邮政储蓄（PS）系统及州级采纳的DI方案，考察银行停业对边境城市对（DI与非DI）中PS存款增长的影响。在邻近银行停业后，（i）非DI-PS办事处的存款相比相邻DI-PS办事处增长七倍，（ii）非DI县每银行的县级存款下降，而相邻DI县则无此现象。两种情况下，该效应在整个1920年代持续减弱，这与DI方案可行性逐渐降低的现象相符。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: Does Deposit Insurance Promote Deposit Stability? Evidence from the Postal Savings System during the 1920s
title_zh: 存款保险是否促进了存款稳定？来自20世纪20年代邮政储蓄系统的证据

abstract: Using a proprietary data set containing nearly 20 million transactions over one and a half years from hundreds of grocery stores, we find evidence of herding among consumers in the use of mobile payment, that is, consumers are more likely to use mobile payment when any previous transaction within 1 min is paid with mobile. The effect of herding is stronger when consumers observe more mobile payment usage within a minute. Further, we find that irrational herding (mimicry) drives the observed herding behavior. Finally, we find that consumers’ price sensitivity and experience in mobile payment mitigate their herding, but the direct network effect does not affect herding.
abstract_zh: 利用一份包含近两千万笔交易、覆盖数百家杂货店一年半时间的专有数据集，我们发现了消费者在移动支付使用中的从众行为证据，即当一分钟内的任何先前交易通过移动支付完成时，消费者更倾向于使用移动支付。当消费者在一分钟内观察到更多移动支付使用时，从众效应更为显著。进一步地，我们发现非理性从众（模仿行为）驱动了所观察到的从众现象。最后，我们发现消费者的价格敏感性和移动支付经验会缓解其从众行为，但直接网络效应并不影响从众。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: Herding in Mobile Payment: Evidence, Mechanism, and Heterogeneity
title_zh: 移动支付中的羊群效应：证据、机制与异质性

abstract: Abstract During the global economic crisis of 1929–33, deposits in the Dutch commercial banking sector sharply declined as funds shifted to the government‐guaranteed Post Office Savings Bank and other savings institutions. Unlike earlier studies for neighbouring countries, we demonstrate that this shift was driven less by a flight to safety and more by a reduction in long‐term interest rates on savings accounts offered by commercial banks, whilst the rates offered by the Post Office Savings Bank remained stable. Through a series of policy measures resembling financial repression, the Dutch government actively encouraged this shift to ensure a steady demand for government debt amongst savings institutions. As the demand for loans decreased, commercial banks managed to retain their profitability by reducing lending to smaller, less profitable businesses, as evidenced by higher minimum loan sizes, a preference for existing clients over new ones, and increased requirements for tangible collateral. This strategic move to eliminate less profitable loans from their portfolios enabled banks to weather the period with minimal damage and prevent an outright banking crisis, but it did contribute to a substantial reduction in private credit.
abstract_zh: 摘要 在1929年至1933年的全球经济危机期间，荷兰商业银行部门的存款急剧下降，资金转向由政府担保的邮政储蓄银行及其他储蓄机构。与先前针对邻国的研究不同，我们证明，这一转变更多是由商业银行储蓄账户长期利率下降所驱动，而非出于避险行为，而邮政储蓄银行提供的利率则保持稳定。通过一系列类似金融压制的政策措施，荷兰政府积极推动这一转变，以确保储蓄机构对政府债务的稳定需求。随着贷款需求减少，商业银行通过减少对较小、利润较低企业的贷款来维持盈利能力，这体现在最低贷款额度的提高、偏好现有客户而非新客户，以及对有形抵押品要求的增加。这一战略性举措，即从投资组合中剔除利润较低的贷款，使银行得以在最小损失下度过该时期，并避免了一场全面的银行业危机，但确实导致了私人信贷的大幅缩减。
title: A series of (un)fortunate events: Commercial bank interest rates and deposit reallocation during the Great Depression in the Netherlands
title_zh: 一系列（不）幸事件：大萧条时期荷兰商业银行利率与存款重新配置
